selection.classification_rationale: Geographer and Marxist urban theorist, with substantial historical studies. Existing urbanhistory roster explicitly identifies the contribution from geography; treat as a theory resource in this selection.

rows.context: Examines capitalist restructuring and place identity; Hayden draws on his account while Massey disputes its treatment of tradition.
rows.works: The Condition of Postmodernity (1989), 302–304; From Space to Place and Back Again (1991), through Hayden

strands.title: Place, tradition and historical change
strands.focus: Massey disputes the necessary association of place identity with fixed tradition; Harvey allows valuable local resistance while questioning its sufficiency.

strands.title: Geographical resources in public history
strands.focus: Hayden uses Harvey while citing Massey’s feminist criticism in a project joining urban landscapes and public memory.

rows.context: Geographer whose urban political economy and historical studies of the city are standard resources for urban historians. A contributor from geography, not a school member.
rows.works: Social Justice and the City (1973); The Condition of Postmodernity (1989)

strands.title: Space, capital and the cultural city
strands.focus: Urban political economy (Harvey), the city of arcades and commodities (Benjamin) and spatial practice (de Certeau) supply the spatial and cultural turn in urban history, beside the entry’s social-science programme. They are resources from geography, criticism and theory, not a school.
strands.works: Social Justice and the City (1973); Das Passagen-Werk (1982); The Practice of Everyday Life (1980/84)

existing_sources_preserved.title: David Harvey, The Condition of Postmodernity (Blackwell, 1989), 302–304.
existing_sources_preserved.citation: David Harvey, The Condition of Postmodernity (Blackwell, 1989), 302–304.

verification.note: Original scan pages 302–304 visually read after discovering the downloaded PDF has no text layer. Harvey links place identity, tradition and flexible accumulation; explicitly says regional resistance can be valuable but cannot bear radical change alone. This qualification remains alongside Massey’s criticism. Page 311 incidentally read while locating pagination. Full book and 1991 UCLA lecture not read; Hayden’s quotations from that lecture are reception evidence, not independent original collation.
